question: What lie at work accidentally spiraled out of control?
story: I became my entire company's top expert on a software I have never once opened. It started in a meeting. My boss asked if anyone knew Salesforce, and I nodded, mostly to look busy. That was the mistake. The next week they made me the Salesforce point person. People started emailing me questions. So every night I would quietly Google the answer, wait an hour, then reply like a wise professor. I ran trainings by reading the help page out loud five minutes early. I got a certificate. I got a raise. They put me on a company newsletter as our resident guru. Two years later a new hire finally asked me to screen share, and I panicked and faked a power outage. I still do not know how to log in. Somehow I am now management. Fake it, I guess.
